title: Language that empowers or disempowers
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:48Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

draft.title: Language that empowers or disempowers
card: The way a group is named and described shapes how readers see it. Word choice can give a group respect and a voice, or take them away.
language names people as capable and as agents who act. It can use the words a group uses for itself, or describe what people do and decide.
language describes people as helpless, as a problem or as objects. It talks about them and not with them. An example is calling teenagers a menace.
These choices have social effects. They can change how a community is treated, what people expect of its members and how its members feel about themselves.
draft.remember: Naming and describing a group can build it up or put it down, and readers feel the effect.

a.q: A council report says, 'Local youth are a menace the town must control.' What effect does this wording most likely have?
opts: It disempowers young people by presenting them as a problem
It empowers young people by giving them a voice in the town
It includes young people by using words such as we and our
It shows low modality by suggesting youth might be a problem
a.why: Calling young people a menace to be controlled presents them as a problem and not as people with a say, so it disempowers them. The inclusion option is tempting, but nothing in the sentence draws young people in.
a.clue: Is the group treated as a problem or as people who act?

b.q: Which sentence about residents of an aged care home in Hobart is most empowering?
opts: Residents voted to choose the home's new weekly activities
Residents are looked after by staff who decide their day
The elderly are a burden on the home's limited resources
The old folk in the home need to be kept happy and quiet
b.why: Residents voted and chose, so they are shown as capable people who make decisions. The sentence about staff deciding the day may sound kind, but it presents residents as people things are done to, which disempowers them.
b.clue: Who is shown making the decisions?

a.best: It disempowers young people by presenting them as a problem

b.best: Residents voted to choose the home's new weekly activities
